q1_issues.issue: One symbol sk_group_1 serves "them" in both clauses, so the parse asserts that the very same things are both available (8) and sealed (16) — the sentence contrasts what different states do with their own copies.
(Member sk_group_1 available) predicates a member-property of the group symbol, which Categorical statements forbids for plurals — it says the group-as-object is available.
(Member sk_group_1 sealed) has the same defect: a property of a plural's members predicated on the group symbol instead of distributed.
"keep" is listed under Theme in Thematic roles (object possessed/held with no change to it), but its object is given Patient.

Both clauses have distributive predicates over plural group subjects (sk_states_1, sk_states_2) but neither emits the per-member Implication rule the grouped-plural form requires alongside the group event.

q2_gaps: an unbound PLURAL pronoun with an inanimate referent ("them" = the records) — Names and casing fixes (GroupOf sk_group_1 person) for plural they with no "salient kind" escape, unlike singular "it"
contrastive "others" as a second, disjoint subset of an earlier plural — no licensed encoding for the disjointness or complement relation; RestOf covers only "the rest of X"
the quantifier word on a plural GROUP subject ("some states") — QuantifierPhrase is defined for kind-level generics and verbal rules, so "some" here goes unrecorded
notes: The two resultative small clauses otherwise follow the state-result shape (Patient, reified state with Experiencer, flat atom, Result link), and "as much as 30 years" -> MeasureAtMost duration is right, as is emitting no tense atom for the habitual present and no connective atom for the semicolon.
